results.title: Why is share market falling? Here are 5 key factors
results.description: New Delhi: Indian stock markets witnessed a sharp selloff on Friday, with the Sensex crashing more than 900 points and the Nifty 50 slipping close to the 23,600 mark amid rising crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions. The 30-share BSE Sensex plunged over 1 per cent to touch an intraday low of 75,474, while the broader NSE Nifty 50 dropped more than 260 points to hit 23,606 during morning trade. Selling was widespread across the market. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices declined by as much as 1.5 per cent during the session. The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies fell to around Rs 471 lakh crore from nearly Rs 477 lakh crore in the previous session, wiping out about Rs 6 lakh crore of investors' wealth. Here are five major factors behind the stock market fall: 1. Crude oil crosses $100 The sharp rise in global crude oil prices emerged as the biggest concern for domestic equities. Brent crude crossed the $100-per-barrel mark for the first time since May amid fears of disruptions to oil supplies and shipping routes. Brent had gained about 13.5 per cent during the week after attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea raised concerns over the movement of energy supplies from West Asia. India imports most of its crude oil requirements. Sustained high prices can increase the country's import bill, weaken the rupee, raise inflation and hurt corporate margins. 2. Escalating US-Iran conflict The continuing conflict between the US and Iran has added to uncertainty across global financial markets. Fresh American strikes and threats of further military action have raised fears of a wider conflict in West Asia. Iran-backed Houthi attacks on shipping routes have also intensified concerns over possible disruptions in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz. The absence of signs of a diplomatic resolution has prompted investors to reduce exposure to riskier assets. 3. US bond yields surge Rising US Treasury yields have further weakened sentiment in global equity markets. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to around 4.71 per cent, its highest level in about 18 months, as rising energy prices revived inflation concerns. Higher bond yields make US debt instruments more attractive and can lead foreign investors to withdraw money from emerging markets such as India. 4. Trump's tariff measures return Renewed trade tensions also weighed on investor confidence after the Donald Trump administration announced tariffs ranging from 10 per cent to 12.5 per cent on imports from 60 trading partners. India has been placed in the lower 10 per cent tariff category. The duties were imposed under Section 301 of the US Trade Act, with the administration citing inadequate enforcement against goods produced through forced labour. The latest measures have raised concerns that higher tariffs could slow global trade, increase US inflation and keep interest rates elevated for longer. 5. Nifty breaches technical support The Nifty's fall below key support levels intensified selling pressure. The index breached the 23,800-23,750 support zone and slipped below 23,700 during intraday trading. According to Bajaj Broking, a sustained break below 23,800 could extend the decline towards the 23,500 level. The brokerage said the outlook would remain cautious below 24,000, while a sustained move above that level would be the first indication of a possible recovery.
